video_title: Why Aggregates Exist: Consistency Boundary, Not a Table
core_insight: An aggregate is a transactional consistency boundary that groups related domain objects under one root so invariants are enforced atomically without locking the whole database.

scenes.voice: Why do we need aggregates at all? Because related objects must stay consistent together.
scenes.visual: Close-up of an Order with items, total, status, payment flickering out of sync.

scenes.voice: An Order has items, a total, a status, a payment. Update them independently and you get a cancelled order with new items, or a total that doesn't match items.
scenes.visual: Split screen showing partial writes leading to invalid state: cancelled + new item, total mismatch.

scenes.voice: The obvious fix is a big database transaction. That works, but it locks a lot and couples services. The other extreme is accept eventual consistency everywhere and write compensating logic for every invariant.
scenes.visual: Scale diagram: big DB transaction covering whole DB vs scattered services with compensations.

scenes.voice: We need a boundary smaller than the whole database and larger than a single row. That's an aggregate: a consistency boundary with one owner.
scenes.visual: Mermaid graph showing Client -> Aggregate Root -> Entities/Value Objects, Repository loads/saves whole graph.
scenes.mermaid:
graph TD
    Client --> AR[Aggregate Root]
    AR --> E1[Entity]
    AR --> E2[Entity]
    AR --> VO[Value Object]
    AR -. enforces invariants .-> State
    Repository -->|load/save whole graph| AR

scenes.voice: All changes go through the root. The root checks the whole graph before mutating. Children are private; nothing outside holds a direct reference to them.
scenes.visual: Animation of addItem() call entering root, root validating total and status, then persisting.

scenes.voice: Trade-off: a larger aggregate means more data loaded per transaction and higher contention. Keep aggregates small and cohesive. For queries, use read models, not the aggregate.
scenes.visual: Size vs contention curve rising with aggregate size, then read model arrow for queries.

scenes.voice: So model aggregates around business transactions, not tables. The aggregate is the unit of consistency, not the unit of persistence.
scenes.visual: Order aggregate example with invariant total == sum(items) and valid status transitions highlighted.

mental_model: Think of an aggregate as a single unit of work with one owner. Load the whole graph, mutate only via the root, persist the whole graph. Use IDs for cross-aggregate references, domain events or sagas for coordination.
final_takeaway: Aggregate is a consistency boundary, not a performance trick. Root enforces invariants; keep it small and use read models for queries.
